newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy pension funds to take off in 1997 -Treu.
newsitem.headline: Italy pension funds to take off in 1997 -Treu.

text.p: Private pension funds should take off in 1997 after years of delays and false starts, Italian Labour Minister Tiziano Treu said on Wednesday.
"If 1996 was the year of preparations, 1997 will be the operative year," Treu told a news conference.
Earlier he signed a ministerial decree which adds further regulations for Italy's nascent pension fund market following guidelines laid down by the Treasury last month.

Details of the decree, which will touch on the professional requirements needed to run the funds and accountancy practices, are due to be published shortly in the official state bulletin and will pass into immediate effect.
Treu said studies showed that tens of trillions of lire would flow into the funds.
Reforms to the Italian pension sector in 1995 removed obstacles to the launch of private pension funds, but the government has spent months working out a regulatory framework for their management.
"You will see that the wait was worth it," Treu said.
Many trade unions, foreign companies, banks and insurance groups have expressed interest in entering the market.
The government is hoping to develop the private pension market in order to reduce the state's vast pension commitments. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
